criteria.text: A new test fixture (two scratch git repos built in a tmp dir by the test itself: repo A holds the manifest+evidence, repo B holds the SHAs) FAILS at the unit's base SHA and PASSES at head.
A regression test (or the existing suite) proves no-flag invocation is unchanged; the #267 escape-refusal test still passes against the evidence root.
Full test suite green at head; python3 scripts/validate.py exit 0.
NEGATIVE CONTROL executed: verify.py change reverted (test kept) -> fixture test RED - recorded via evidence-run.py.

intent.goal: Let one verify.py invocation reach two authorities: evidence paths bounded under one root, SHA/git operations run against another, so a chained-run manifest can be verified at all.
intent.ruled_out: Threading the roots through ~25 call sites as parameters (large diff, no behavioural gain); making --evidence-root default to the --git-dir toplevel (would silently move the #267 bound when only the SHA leg was redirected); relaxing the bound to an unversioned directory (that IS the #267 hole, not a fix for it); teaching the manifest to name its own roots (a manifest cannot choose what judges it).
intent.why: AC-1/AC-2 demand a cross-repo manifest verify while single-root behaviour stays byte-identical and #267's refusals survive re-rooting; _ROOTS defaults of None make the unflagged path the same code it was.

negative_control.did: checked out head_sha in a throwaway worktree, restored runtime/scripts/verify.py from base_sha (git checkout a58bf71a -- runtime/scripts/verify.py) and left the new test in place; then ran the bound command again in a second, untouched worktree at head_sha
negative_control.result: RED under the control: exit 1, 8 ASSERTION FAILURES in CrossRepoRoots (mutant KILLED). GREEN at clean head_sha: exit 0, 255 tests. The one case that survives the control is test_without_the_split_the_same_manifest_cannot_verify, which asserts the PRE-split behaviour and is meant to hold on both sides.
